name: vImage (vImageScale_ARGB8888)
baseline: UIGraphicsImageRenderer drawing a UIImage(contentsOfFile:) into a smaller context
verdict_reason: In the only end-to-end published comparison found, resizing a 12,000 px JPEG from disk took 2.3126 s with vImage against 0.1420 s with UIGraphicsImageRenderer, about 16x slower, because the vImage path decodes the full-resolution image into a buffer before scaling. The result says nothing about already-decoded pixel buffers.
tier_reason: Independent measurement (NSHipster) with public code and the device and OS stated, run in the Debug test configuration.
claimed_speedup: No speedup measured: vImage 2.3126 s vs UIKit 0.1420 s (16.3x slower, derived from page data).
workload: Load a 12,000 px square, 20 MB JPEG from disk, scale it to 100 x 100 and return a UIImage; average of XCTest measure() iterations.
toolchain: Swift 5.0; Debug test configuration in the example project's scheme
one_liner: Accelerate's SIMD image scaler; resizing a JPEG from disk was 16x slower than UIGraphicsImageRenderer in an iPhone 7 test.
how_it_is_fast: vImageScale_ARGB8888 is a SIMD-vectorized CPU resampler. In this test its speed is beside the point: the vImage path calls CGImageSourceCreateImageAtIndex and vImageBuffer_InitWithCGImage, which decode and copy all 144 million source pixels before scaling begins, while the UIKit path does not pay that full cost.
use_it_when: You already hold decoded pixel buffers (camera frames, editing pipelines) and need high-quality resampling
Batch processing inside a pipeline already built on Accelerate
skip_it_when: Making thumbnails from encoded JPEG, HEIC or PNG files: UIKit and Image I/O were 14x to 16x faster in the published test
caveats: Debug test configuration; the timed work is mostly inside Accelerate and ImageIO
Decode and scale are timed together; the scaling step alone was not measured
tradeoffs: Verbose C API: buffer allocation, pixel formats and error codes by hand
Needs the whole decoded image in memory first

evidence.quote: performed on an iPhone 7 running iOS 12.2,
the extra work necessary to use the low-level Accelerate APIs probably isn't justified in most circumstances.
